meaning: Titles and reading notes drafted by an AI agent in the register of the paper they annotate. No mathematician has reviewed them.

notes.Breakdown.FundSol.integrable_kernelSecon: The source must vanish at the evaluation point. This cancellation makes the Hessian-kernel expression an ordinary integrable function.
notes.Breakdown.FundSol.kernel: Lean gives inverse zero a total value. The smoothness and differential kernel identities are proved away from the origin.
notes.Breakdown.FundSol.secondPartial_potentia: The vanishing-source hypothesis is part of this pointwise formula and must be retained when using it.
notes.Breakdown.GradientBoundedOn: The name mentions the gradient, but the predicate also bounds the velocity itself by the same constant on the closed interval.
notes.Breakdown.NoBoundedSmoothSolution: The excluded solution has one energy bound for the entire time domain. A bound on each shorter interval alone does not supply that hypothesis.
notes.Breakdown.SmoothFlow.IsSolenoidalSymbol: This predicate includes conjugate symmetry, which ensures a real physical field, as well as the frequency-divergence condition.
notes.Breakdown.SmoothFlow.pressureSymbol: The formula uses total complex division at zero frequency. The later identification with the bilinear pressure symbol is stated almost everywhere.
notes.Breakdown.SmoothFlow.toL2C: This conversion returns zero when the input does not belong to L2. Its representative identities assume L2 membership.
notes.Breakdown.SmoothFlow.toWeightL1: This conversion is a total function with a zero fallback outside weighted L1. The subsequent representation lemmas assume the required L1 membership.
notes.Breakdown.WeakProfile.ContinuousVarConst: Continuity is asserted on the interval beginning at the chosen initial time, including that initial endpoint and excluding the terminal endpoint.
notes.Breakdown.WeakProfile.PairingDilate: This definition is an implication from the velocity-pairing interface. Its named discharge proves that entire implication.
notes.Breakdown.WeakProfile.SliceIntegrand: The interface retains the velocity-pairing and advection-by-parts premises used to identify the weak integrand.
notes.Breakdown.WeakProfile.SliceMeasurable: The velocity-pairing interface is an explicit antecedent of this measurability interface.
notes.Breakdown.WeakProfile.TrilinearDilate: This definition is an implication from the weak-gradient interface. Its named discharge retains that premise.
notes.Breakdown.WeakProfile.VarConstGood: The interface assumes both bilinear integrability and the scalar variation-of-constants identity.
notes.Breakdown.WeakProfile.VarConstInner: The interface assumes bilinear integrability and uses a strictly positive heat regularization parameter.
notes.Breakdown.eq_of_isSolutionOn: Both solutions have bounded energy on the comparison interval. The velocity-and-gradient bound is required for the designated comparison solution.
notes.Breakdown.tendsto_integral_pressureDefec: The averaging radius tends to infinity in this argument. These mollifiers are used to average over larger regions.
